answer: Admission requires each new key to plant a non-transferable timber claim and anchor a bond against it in a public registry maintained by already-established operators. The applicant must then emit a unique weekly signal: a signed receipt of unpaid work assigned by three non-adjacent operators who countersign only original results. If two identities share an operator key, their timber claims collide and both anchored bonds are slashed. Until six consecutive signals are countersigned, rewards stay unwithdrawable, so a farm cannot mint many full shares from one wallet.
